status: FAIL at unchanged budgets; first-order SPEC 5.0 lag model, NOT a compiler exposure run and NOT a qualification

measured.route_segments: 41..67 (polyline 20.031..33.496 mm at <= 500 um per stage); pin Manhattan 16.38..29.84 mm = 32..59 raw stages

model: lag = max(0, H + 1/b - lead/c), b = c = 64 words/cycle, local lead Qwen 16 / DS 28 cycles (SPEC 5.0)
findings: The 12/11-cycle hop price assumed about 9 relay stages (<= 5 mm). The native die_v12 ring edges are 20..33.5 mm, so even a plain registered relay chain is 44..70 cycles a hop (3.7..5.8x the price) before any elastic storage.

The D8 elastic station adds 4 forward edges per segment: 168..272 cycles a hop (14..22.7x). One exposed one-hop remote record costs 152..256 (Qwen) / 140..244 (DS) cycles: a single record exceeds the Qwen 93-cycle layer budget, two exceed the DS 290-cycle budget.
A remote read round trip over the diagonal is 2 x 2 x H + 4 = 676..1,092 cycles against 50.
Throughput (II 1) is not the problem; latency is. The budgets are not raised and no row is re-priced.
structural_options_not_yet_evaluated: Shorten the edges: SID order SW0/SE1/NW2/NE3 puts two diagonals on the ring; a geometric order (SW,SE,NE,NW) removes both diagonals and roughly halves the worst edge. Needs the compiler's slice map and the die lead.
One forward edge per segment: registered relays between elastic stations placed only every k-th segment (credit loop depth 2k+margin <= D), so a hop is about S + 4*S/k cycles.

Compiler lead: schedule every cross-slice push at least H cycles before its first reader (exposure 0 when lead >= H); needs the real B2 vectors (b2c/vec) through tools/hgi_e2e/b2.py traffic with ring_hop_cycles set to the measured H.
next_gate: tools/hgi_e2e/b2.py traffic on the current B2 Qwen and DS vectors with ring_hop_cycles = measured H per edge; pass only at <= 93 / <= 290 exposed
